title: Microbes in Human Welfare
seo_title: Microbes in Human Welfare Class 12 Biology Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 8)
standard_code: Class 12 Biology, Chapter 8: Microbes in Human Welfare
standard_text: Microbes in food processing, industrial production, sewage treatment, energy generation and microbes as bio-control agents and bio-fertilizers. Antibiotics; production and judicious use.
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 12 Biology worksheets for NCERT Chapter 8 Microbes in Human Welfare: microbes in household foods, industrial products, antibiotics, sewage treatment, biogas, biocontrol agents and biofertilisers. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Microbes make curd, bread, cheese, antibiotics, enzymes and biogas.
key_sub: Biofertilisers and biocontrol agents reduce chemical use.
body_html:
How to think about it

Lactobacillus turns milk into curd, yeast makes dough rise and gives alcohol, and other microbes make cheeses. Industries use microbes to make acids (citric, acetic, lactic), enzymes (lipases, streptokinase), antibiotics such as penicillin, cyclosporin A and statins.

In sewage treatment, aerobic bacteria in flocs lower the BOD, and anaerobic bacteria in digesters make biogas, mostly methane. Biocontrol agents such as Bt, Trichoderma and baculoviruses control pests; biofertilisers such as Rhizobium, Azotobacter, cyanobacteria and mycorrhizae enrich the soil.

Example

Microbe for curd?

lactic acid bacteria

Answer: Lactobacillus

Example

Main gas in biogas?

from methanogens

Answer: methane

Common mistakes

  • Saying biogas is mostly CO₂.
  • Calling Rhizobium a biocontrol agent.
  • Thinking wine is distilled.
